utility_optimization.requested_by_operator: utility × FMEA × criticality × STPA × operational use
utility_optimization.formula: Q = U × F × C × T × O

U.name: utility
U.meaning: Marginal operator outcome or avoided loss delivered by closing this gap

anchors.1: Minor convenience with a verified workaround
anchors.3: Material improvement to a named operator journey
anchors.5: Restores or protects a mission-essential outcome

F.name: FMEA
F.meaning: Canonical severity-preserving FMEA band from raw S/O/Det, never an invented incident rate

C.name: criticality
C.meaning: Canonical criticality factor grounded in consequence and service obligation

T.name: STPA
T.meaning: Canonical unsafe-control significance covering not_provided, provided_unsafe, wrong_timing and duration

O.name: operational_use
O.meaning: Observed affected actors, workflow frequency and mandatory incident/recovery use

anchors.5: Continuous operational path or required incident/recovery path

utility_optimization.canonical_relationship: Retain canonical C×T×F×Dependency×Impact score and class. Q is an explicit operator-value view within admissible ready work; it does not bypass safety classes, dependency gates or compulsory low-frequency recovery tests.
utility_optimization.uncertainty: If any factor is unknown, Q is null with product interval. Do not turn absent usage into zero value or infer production frequency from fixtures.
utility_optimization.cost_control: Among equally admissible comparable-value work, prefer earlier risk reduction per bounded worker-hour/token; report confidence and cost separately rather than disguising cost as safety evidence.
utility_optimization.update_policy: T00 gathers usage and utility evidence; T03 freezes reviewed scores before dispatch; update after failures, changes or stale evidence. Authoring phase has no measured campaign Q.
